ops.title: init's per-user registry write must sit with provisionRepository, not ahead of the local-only steps
ops.body:
Caught 2026-07-30 by the pre-release audit for v0.50.0, fixed before the tag.

Phase D step 3 (cb1f27e) put ccnhome.RecordWorktree at internal/cli/sync.go:62 —
after ccsync.Install had already written the refspecs, but BEFORE the
"initialized:" line, the .claude/settings.json registration, the reconcile CI
workflow, and the post-merge hook. Being fatal, an unusable ~/.cc-notes aborted
init there and cost the caller every one of those local-only steps, with the
refspecs already on disk and nothing printed.

That contradicted the principle the same function states at sync.go:95-97, about
the capt-hook calls: "a failure here never blocks the local-only refspecs, plugin
registration, CI workflow, or post-merge hook above." v0.49.0 honored it — its
only out-of-repo write was provisionRepository, which runs after all of them.

Fix: move the RecordWorktree call down beside provisionRepository. It stays
fatal — this is a reordering, not error-swallowing, so a genuinely broken state
root still reports loudly, just without eating the local work first.

Pinned by TestInitCompletesLocalWiringWhenTheStateRootIsUnusable
(internal/cli/sync_test.go). It points CC_NOTES_HOME at a path under a regular
file so MkdirAll fails with ENOTDIR, then asserts the refspec line and the
plugin registration both survive the error. Litmus verified: with the old
ordering restored the test fails with `init output "" lost the refspec line` and
a missing settings.json.

Gotcha for anyone writing a similar test: initRepo (internal/cli/cli_test.go:133)
sets CC_NOTES_HOME to a fresh t.TempDir(), so a t.Setenv before the fixture is
silently overwritten. Set the state root AFTER the fixture.
